newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end slightly higher on firm cash.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end slightly higher on firm cash.

text.p: NYMEX October Henry Hub natgas futures settled slightly higher Thursday because of firm Gulf cash prices, but most other months were lower, industry sources said.

October ended 0.7 cent higher at $1.813 per million British thermal units after hitting a high of $1.855 this morning. November finished 1.2 cents lower at $2.018. The Oct/Nov spread widened to 20.5 cents.
"Cash was once again the key factor today. We thought cash was going to soften, but it didn't. This is what gave support to the market," said one futures trader.
Traders pegged support in October in the high-$1.70s, then the $1.73-1.74 area. Further support was seen at $1.68. Traders said resistance was at $1.913, Tuesday's high.
In anticipation of softer cash prices ahead of the weekend, most traders said they expected a retest of the $1.74 level on Friday.
However, October's ability to bounce off the low and close the gap may give the market the support it needs, other traders said.

Boosted by a high storage demand, cash prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes were talked in the low-to-mid $1.80s, steady to one cent higher on the day. Midcontinent prices were also stable in the mid-$1.60s to about $1.70. At the New York city-gate, gas sold in the low-$2 area.
NYMEX said an estimated 30,084 Henry Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 34,373. The 12-month strip slipped 0.8 cent to $2.005.
NYMEX's October Permian contract wavered only slightly today to finish unchanged at $1.53. An estimated 33 contracts traded.
On the physical side, prices fell more than five cents to the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s.
On the KBCT, October held its lead to settle 2.9 cents higher at $1.625. The East/West spread widened by a half-cent to 20.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
-- H McCulloch, New York Power Desk +212-859-1628
